issues.description: The type of Person.birthday is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and the template repository define Person.birthday as a LocalDate (teaching the student to use LocalDate in UI and service code), but the solution repository's common Person class declares birthday as a String. Furthermore, the solution's client code (PersonScene) still treats birthday as a LocalDate (e.g. setting DatePicker value from person.getBirthday()). This mismatch (String vs LocalDate) is a structural type incompatibility that will cause confusion and runtime/serialization issues (clients expect LocalDate but the model is String) and prevents students from following the intended design using LocalDate.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the birthday field type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably restore Person.birthday to java.time.LocalDate in the solution repository's common model (matching the problem statement and template). Update any serialization/deserialization configuration if needed (e.g. ensure Jackson is configured to handle LocalDate ISO formats) so the client and server exchange LocalDate correctly. Alternatively, if a String is intended, update the problem statement and all client code (DatePicker usage, bindings, and comparisons) to work with String and provide clear conversion utilities — but aligning everything to LocalDate is recommended to preserve the intended design and avoid student confusion.
